reason: Opening sentence of the developer guide states stateful, managed network firewall and IDS/IPS service for your VPC.
Quote is the continuation of the Allow bullet that states the denial of non-matching traffic; it limits the denial to default action order and excludes strict order.
Quote states domain name stateful inspection with allow lists and deny lists that the stateful engine looks for.
Quota row in the cannot-be-changed table gives 10,000,000 domain specifications per firewall policy across Marketplace managed domain rule groups.
Quotes give the default HOME_NET of the deployment VPC CIDR, that only that range is filtered, and that traffic from other VPCs via a transit gateway needs HOME_NET set manually.
Quote states SNI for HTTPS, Host header for HTTP, no out-of-band DNS lookups, and not IP addresses.
Both quotes state the endpoint cannot protect its own subnet and that firewall subnets are reserved for Network Firewall only.
Quote states per-AZ installation, one subnet per AZ for the primary endpoint, and VPC endpoint associations for more.
FAQ under TLS inspection states all cipher suites supported by ACM are supported.
Quotes give the two deployment types and centralized as a TGW VPC attachment, but 'distributed, inside each VPC' appears only in an unquoted context sentence.
FAQ quote states a dedicated subnet with a minimum size of /28.
FAQ quote states import of rules in common open source formats or compatible partner rules.
FAQ quote states deep packet inspection for encrypted traffic is supported.
FAQ quote states all traffic routed to the endpoint is inspected and routing is the path-insertion mechanism.
Quotes state IPS with signature-based detection and web filtering for known-bad URLs and FQDN monitoring.
Quotes state managed service for VPC protections that scales automatically with no infrastructure to manage.
FAQ quote lists the four outbound control types exactly.
FAQ quote matches the claim word for word.
FAQ quote states pricing by number of firewalls and amount of traffic inspected.
Quotes state regional service and suggest Firewall Manager for multi-account policy and governance.
FAQ quote states thousands of rules based on domain, port, protocol, IP addresses and pattern matching.
FAQ quote states an SLA with 99.99% uptime commitment.
Quotes define stateless rules as ACLs on IPs, ports or protocols and stateful rules as maintaining connections or sessions.
Quote under the TGW question states native integration or manual VPC attachment.
Quote under the encrypted traffic section states TLS 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 except ECH and ESNI.
Quote states perimeter filtering including internet gateway, NAT gateway, VPN and Direct Connect.
Quotes support country-code matching, source/destination filtering and IPv4/IPv6, but use with Suricata rule strings and standard stateful rule groups is only in an unquoted context sentence.
Quote is a bullet directly under the lead-in 'When a firewall owner's account becomes inactive' and states FAIL_CLOSED dropping all traffic on both endpoint kinds.
Quota row in the cannot-be-changed table gives 5 IP set references per Suricata compatible stateful rule group.

Quote gives only the revoked/disabled/deleted causes; 'cannot process traffic until restored' is an unquoted bullet, and the scope 'customer managed key' is not stated (page says the key used by the firewall owner).
Quotes support same or different destination per log type, but neither quote names Amazon S3, CloudWatch Logs or Data Firehose as the destinations.
Quotes define flow, alert (DROP, ALERT, REJECT) and TLS logs and limit logging to traffic forwarded to the stateful engine.
Quote supports predefined AWS-maintained rules and most at no additional cost, but the three group kinds (active threat defense, domain and IP, threat signature) appear only in unquoted context.
Quote supports the waiver in a service chain in your account, but 'one-to-one with Network Firewall usage' and the same-Region and same-path condition are only in unquoted context.
Quotes state no asymmetric routing support and that traffic must reach the same endpoint in both directions.
Quotes support the TLS endpoint limits, but the main claim 'you cannot share a firewall policy that uses TLS inspection' is in the unquoted preceding sentence.
FAQ quote states not for volumetric DDoS and recommends DDoS best practices and Shield Advanced.
Quota rows in the cannot-be-changed table give required 1 policy per firewall and at most 1,000 firewalls per policy.
Quotes support own and AWS-managed rule groups and stateless or stateful types, but the definition 'reusable set of criteria' is only in an unquoted context sentence.
Quotes give per-GB billing and $0.065 for 1 GB, but the US East (N. Virginia) scope and 'regardless of source or destination' condition are only in unquoted context.
